name: Handmade jewelry business
blurb: Make and sell handmade jewelry online, at markets and through local shops
title: Jewelry Business: How to Start Selling Handmade Jewelry
description: How to start a handmade jewelry business: how it makes money, the tools and materials you need, metal safety rules, who it suits and how to test it first.
h1: How to start a handmade jewelry business
answer: A handmade jewelry business makes earrings, necklaces, rings or bracelets and sells them online, at markets or through local shops. It can start small with modest tools and materials, but competition is heavy, photography and marketing take as much time as making, and some places have rules on metals like nickel and lead.

sections.h: How a jewelry business makes money
body: You earn the difference between the price of each piece and its materials, packaging, shipping, marketplace or payment fees, and your time. Custom orders, personalised pieces and wholesale to shops are common extra income.
Making time is the cost people underprice most. Market stall fees, returns and ad spend can take much of the rest.

ul: Tools and materials for your technique: beading, wirework, metal smithing or resin each need different kit and skills.

Materials you can trust, with clear metal content. Skin-contact jewelry is regulated in some places: the EU limits nickel release, and in the US children's products, including jewelry, are limited to 100 ppm lead in accessible parts.
Good photos, a shop on a marketplace or your own site, and packaging.
Business registration and tax setup where you live; check local rules.
Product liability insurance if you sell at markets or to shops.

sections.h: Who it suits (and who it doesn't)

head: Suits
Not for
rows: Makers with a distinct style and steady hands
People hoping to resell cheap generic pieces
People willing to photograph, post and market weekly
Anyone who wants to make but never sell
Those who can start small alongside a job

ul: Saturation: marketplaces are full of jewelry, so a clear style matters.
Underpricing your time, which makes growth impossible.
Material safety: using unknown metals can lead to allergy complaints or breaking local rules.
Copying: designs get copied; well-known brand designs are not yours to copy either.
Platform dependence: marketplace rule or fee changes can hit sales fast.

sections.h: How to test it cheaply first

ol: Make ten pieces in one style with materials you already have or can buy cheaply.
Show them to people outside your friends and ask what they would pay.
List a few pieces on one marketplace and watch views and saves.
Take a table at one local market or craft fair.
Cost each piece fully, including your hours and fees, before setting prices.
Pick one technique and a small, consistent collection.
Source materials with known metal content from reliable suppliers.
Register the business and set aside money for tax.
Open one sales channel and post work regularly.
Track sales, materials and hours per piece, and drop designs that do not sell.

faq.q: Can I start a jewelry business from home?
faq.a: Usually yes for making and selling online, though some places require registration, and metal work with heat or chemicals needs safe ventilation. Check local rules.

faq.q: Where should I sell handmade jewelry first?
faq.a: One marketplace or one local market is enough to start. Add channels once you know which pieces sell and at what price.

faq.q: Do I need to worry about nickel or lead?
faq.a: Yes, especially for earrings, skin-contact pieces and children's jewelry. The EU limits nickel release and the US limits lead in children's products. Buy materials with clear content from suppliers you trust.
